about: COCOLO 0.4.0 strict lifecycle end-to-end requirements (PLAN-0.4.0.md T7). Every requirement names the checks in scripts/e2e_lifecycle.py that prove it; a requirement with no check, or a check naming no requirement, fails tests/test_e2e_requirements.py.

requirements.statement: A fresh install through the scripted setup (S1 answers file and passphrase) finishes with every step ok, the protected command rule installed and the collector ready.
Setup run again on an installed project changes nothing: same files, same digests, no new records except its own checks.
The owner key is configured; a wrong passphrase is refused with its fixed reason and changes nothing.
Replacing the owner key refuses signatures made with the old key and accepts the new one's.
provider-observe succeeds for both fake clients, and the Claude billing probe succeeds.
Billing attestation is recorded and admission accepts it.

Paid usage on is refused with paid_usage_usable; an API key in the environment with provider_api_key_present; an unreviewed client version with client_version_unreviewed; a signed-out client with observation_unavailable.
Routing for a Codex primary and a Claude primary returns the policy's role, model, effort, agent and sandbox, and the child runs with exactly those.
A route edited after learning-route is refused.
For each primary, readiness, assignment and result preflight and export preflight pass.

Open, dispatch, validate (with one structural repair on a native path where one applies) and record the result succeed; the worker's answer values match the oracle and each required evidence outcome is pass or observed.

The verifier opened for the worker's outcome digest passes every required evidence item with no discrepancy and verdict pass or ready; operational checks pass and QA records accepted: true; the orchestration closes and its report is right.
A child that tries to read outside its export, write anywhere or use the network is stopped, and its result says so.
Uncommitted read paths are refused before admission.
learning-cancel-run stops a running child; it ends cancelled with its capacity released.
A child that goes silent is stopped at the cutoff (controllable clock) and ends with work_silence and its capacity released.
A hard timeout stops a child and ends it with the right terminal state and released capacity.
Killing the project service mid-run: the next service settles the run (run_lost), frees its slot and records nothing twice.
Killing the collector mid-run: the same, once it is back.
Two children at once run; a third is refused with claim_busy and the probe with probe_busy.
Capacity is released after each terminal, shown by a supported per-run read.
Two projects share one collector, each with its own runs and capacity.
Hook events are ingested with recording on and not with it off (S2).
The learning history moves to the project store; learning-run-cycle runs.
Retention removes expired raw events and keeps their summaries (controllable clock).
learning-backup-project and learning-verify-backup succeed.
A failed upgrade forced part-way leaves the records unchanged, learning-rollback works and the next attempt succeeds.
From each earlier release tag (v0.3.1 on), with history built on it, an update to HEAD succeeds and the full run passes again.
A one-command update with an admitted-never-launched run and 0.2.x leftovers present needs no manual stop.
An update with a child really running refuses plainly and changes nothing.
An update with uncommitted managed files is refused.
A second project updated after the first works (no other project stops working).

History built on an earlier release with more than 512 admission records, runs left by 0.2.x and a project over 128 MiB still opens, dispatches and upgrades (the four live-test bugs: unbounded admission history, a masked busy probe, 0.2.x leftovers blocking updates, a protected copy without role files).

A dispatch refused at its claim on a project with long history closes by itself, and after an update from the release before, the next service closes any such run an earlier version left (0.3.3 C2, C3, C3f).
A session with danger-full-access, an unknown host, or opened above the project is refused with its reason.
The protected copy refuses a project it is not bound to.
learning-status, learning-run-status, earlier_version_runs and learning-orchestration-report give the right values at each phase, and none is private.
learning-delete-project removes the project's records and services and leaves another project untouched.
Every step exits 0, or refuses with a reason the step expects; a bare run_unavailable, account_unavailable or probe_unavailable is a failure.
Worker: every answer value matches the oracle; each required evidence outcome is pass or observed.
Verifier: opened for the worker's digest; each required evidence outcome is pass; no discrepancy; verdict pass or ready.
Operational QA: accepted: true.
Capacity: after close, a supported per-run read shows every claimed run released, and the next billing probe gets a slot; final statistics show zero active or pending runs.
An update never needs the collector stopped by hand, and finishes with the collector healthy on the new build.
Records keep their history across every update: counts by kind, never content.
No private value appears in any output: keys, fingerprints, paths under the temporary HOME.
A content-free JSON report with phases, seconds, reason codes and pass or fail per requirement is written, kept as the CI artifact.
